segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I’ve got the final scope in front of me: 38 full users, 12 read-only users, and about 1,450 gauges and torque tools in the first upload. Is that still right?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s right. We may add four inspectors in April, but for the first go-live, 38 and 12 is the number.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. The annual subscription comes to $28,740, and implementation is $5,800 one-time. That includes the asset import, two admin trainings, and the calibration due-date rules we talked through for the Ohio plant.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. On the invoice, can you split it so subscription hits our quality budget and implementation hits the plant project code?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, we can do two line items on one invoice with those descriptions. Payment terms are net 30, and the contract term would run February 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. I need the order form to show the go-live target as March 9. Our audit is the week of April 20, so I don’t want this drifting.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. I’ll put March 9 as the target go-live, with admin training on February 18 and end-user training the week of March 2. If you sign by next Friday, February 6, those dates are held.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. One more thing: our purchasing manager asked whether unused read-only seats can be converted to full seats midterm.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: They can. If you convert them, we just bill the prorated difference for the remaining months. No change to the renewal date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, send it over to me and copy Luis in purchasing. If the insurance language is the same as the draft, I think we’re fine.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send the order form and the insurance exhibit this afternoon, and I’ll include the project code fields on the invoice instructions.
